topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text: My lord, a strange tale did I hear from a passing merchant, and it’s made the soil in my throat dry as summer wheat. He spoke of a man in a far town whose horse—a beast as proud and strong as any, likened to the gift of Saint Christopher—was one day spirited away from his own stable. No thief in the night, but by the very hands of the law, they say. The man sought answers, begging from door to door, his face as twisted as the gnarled oak by the village well. The merchant said the man must find a way to speak with those in power, but I pray, my lord, that such a dark day never comes to our humble fields. May the saints protect us all.
